steps.title: Import React, useState, useRef, and useEffect
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useRef, and useEffect from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all four items from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, useState, useRef, and useEffect from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React hooks for list virtualization are imported.
successCriteria: React, useState, useRef, and useEffect are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported all the necessary React hooks for building a virtualized list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure to import all four items: React, useState, useRef, and useEffect from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React, useState, useRef, and useEffect from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main VirtualList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named VirtualList that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called VirtualList that returns JSX containing a <div> tag.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React, useState, useRef, and useEffect from 'react'

// Create the VirtualList component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component named VirtualList is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The code defines a function or arrow function named VirtualList that returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the VirtualList component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named VirtualList that returns a <div>.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a component called VirtualList that returns a div element.

steps.title: Initialize state for scroll position
steps.instruction: Inside your VirtualList component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called scrollTop initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState with an initial value of 0 and destructure the returned array into scrollTop and setScrollTop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a counter state
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a scrollTop state variable that tracks the current scroll position, starting at 0.
successCriteria: The VirtualList component contains a useState call that creates a scrollTop state variable initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the scrollTop state. This will track how far the user has scrolled in the virtual list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a state variable named scrollTop with an initial value of 0 inside the VirtualList component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the VirtualList component, use useState to create a state variable called scrollTop initialized to 0.

steps.title: Create a ref for the container element
steps.instruction: Inside your VirtualList component, use the useRef hook to create a ref named containerRef that will hold the container DOM element.
steps.hint: Call useRef with null as the initial value and assign it to a variable named containerRef.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a ref for a DOM element
const inputRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: A containerRef variable is created using useRef, ready to be attached to a container element.
successCriteria: The containerRef is declared inside the component using useRef(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a ref that will allow you to access the container DOM element directly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useRef with null as the initial value and naming it containerRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a ref using the useRef hook inside the component.

steps.title: Define configuration constants
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualList component, define three constants: itemHeight set to 50, totalItems set to 1000, and visibleItems set to 10.
steps.hint: Use const declarations with descriptive names and assign numeric values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have three constants defined that will be used for virtualization calculations.
successCriteria: Constants itemHeight, totalItems, and visibleItems are defined with the specified numeric values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the key configuration parameters needed for virtualization.
steps.feedbackPartial: You defined some constants, but make sure you have all three: itemHeight (50), totalItems (1000), and visibleItems (10).
steps.feedbackWrong: Try defining three constants with the exact names and values specified in the instruction.

steps.title: Create the scroll handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the VirtualList component, create a function named handleScroll that updates the scrollTop state with the current scroll position of the container element.
steps.hint: The function should get the current scrollTop value from containerRef.current and call setScrollTop with that value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleScroll function is defined inside the component that updates the scrollTop state when called.
successCriteria: The handleScroll function is defined, accesses containerRef.current.scrollTop, and calls setScrollTop with that value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the scroll handler function that will update the state when the container scrolls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it updates the scrollTop state with containerRef.current.scrollTop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleScroll function is missing or doesn't properly update the scrollTop state.

steps.title: Calculate visible range of items
steps.instruction: Inside your VirtualList component, calculate the startIndex and endIndex based on the scrollTop state. Use the formula: startIndex = Math.floor(scrollTop / itemHeight) and endIndex = startIndex + visibleItems.
steps.hint: You'll need to use the scrollTop state variable and the itemHeight and visibleItems constants you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have startIndex and endIndex variables calculated from the current scroll position.
successCriteria: startIndex is calculated as Math.floor(scrollTop / itemHeight) and endIndex is calculated as startIndex + visibleItems.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully calculated which items should be visible based on the scroll position.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct variables: scrollTop, itemHeight, and visibleItems.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculation isn't quite right. Remember: startIndex = Math.floor(scrollTop / itemHeight) and endIndex = startIndex + visibleItems.

steps.title: Generate visible items array
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a visibleItemsArray using Array.from() with length (endIndex - startIndex) and map each element to create an object with id and content properties.
steps.hint: Use Array.from({ length: endIndex - startIndex }) to create an array of the correct size, then .map() to generate objects with id and content.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a visibleItemsArray variable containing objects with id and content properties for the visible range.
successCriteria: visibleItemsArray is created using Array.from() with length (endIndex - startIndex) and maps to objects with id and content properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the array of visible items with proper id and content properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use Array.from() with the correct length and map to objects with both id and content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visible items array wasn't created correctly. Use Array.from() with length (endIndex - startIndex) and map to create objects with id and content.

steps.title: Add the main container structure
steps.instruction: Return a div element from your component with ref={containerRef}, onScroll={handleScroll}, and inline styles for height, overflow, and border.
steps.hint: The container div should be scrollable and have a fixed height. Use the ref and handler you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a scrollable div container with the ref and scroll handler attached, ready to hold virtualized items.
successCriteria: The component returns a div with ref={containerRef}, onScroll={handleScroll}, and inline styles for height, overflow, and border.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the scrollable container that will hold your virtualized list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the div has ref={containerRef}, onScroll={handleScroll}, and the required inline styles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container structure is missing or incorrect. Check that you're returning a div with the ref, handler, and styles.

steps.title: Add inner spacer element
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add a div element with inline style setting its height to totalItems * itemHeight to create proper scroll height.
steps.hint: Calculate the total height by multiplying totalItems by itemHeight, then set this as the height style of the inner div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have an inner div that provides the correct total scrollable height based on the number of items and their height.
successCriteria: A div element is added inside the container with style={{ height: totalItems * itemHeight }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added the spacer element that gives the container the proper scroll height.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a div, but check if its height is set correctly using totalItems * itemHeight.
steps.feedbackWrong: The spacer element is missing or incorrect. Add a div with style={{ height: totalItems * itemHeight }} inside the container.

steps.title: Render the visible items
steps.instruction: Inside the component, map through the visibleItemsArray to render each visible item as a div positioned absolutely with top based on its index.
steps.hint: Use the map method on visibleItemsArray to return a div for each item. Set the top style to itemHeight * index and include the item content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The visible items will be rendered inside the spacer div, each positioned correctly based on its index.
successCriteria: visibleItemsArray is mapped to render div elements with absolute positioning and correct top values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the visible items with proper positioning.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that each item div has a key, uses absolute positioning, and calculates top correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visible items are not rendered correctly. Ensure you map through visibleItemsArray and return a div for each item with appropriate styles.

steps.title: Add useEffect to log virtualization metrics
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook that logs the startIndex, endIndex, and visibleItemsArray.length to the console whenever scrollTop changes.
steps.hint: Place the useEffect inside your component, after the visibleItemsArray calculation. The dependency array should include scrollTop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect will log the current start index, end index, and number of visible items to the console each time the user scrolls, demonstrating how virtualization reduces the number of rendered items.
successCriteria: A useEffect hook is added that logs startIndex, endIndex, and visibleItemsArray.length when scrollTop changes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The useEffect hook is correctly logging virtualization metrics. You can now scroll in the preview and watch the console to see how only a small subset of items are rendered at any time.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a useEffect, but it might not be logging all three metrics or might have incorrect dependencies. Make sure it logs startIndex, endIndex, and visibleItemsArray.length, and includes scrollTop in the dependency array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook is missing or doesn't log the required metrics. Add a useEffect that logs startIndex, endIndex, and visibleItemsArray.length when scrollTop changes.
